newsitem.title: JAPAN: Volcker calls for target zone for forex stability.
newsitem.headline: Volcker calls for target zone for forex stability.

text.p: A currency management system with specific target zones, and massive intervention if necessary, could effectively stabilise currency markets, former U.S. Federal Reserve governor Paul Volcker told a symposium in Tokyo on Friday.
"We need to make progress to more durable stability...to avoid exchange rates swings, (especially) in the dollar, yen and mark," he said.
He proposed a cooperative system in which currencies would fluctuate within plus or minus 10 percent around a central point, with central bank intervention if needed to defend this.

In addition, Volcker said, countries taking part in the system would agree to modify their monetary policy if necessary to reinforce any intervention, with everything done under supervision from the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
He acknowledged that absolute exchange rate stability was impossible, but said this system would avoid more extreme fluctuations "of 20, 30, even 40 percent, as has happened".
The dollar has fluctuated wildly over the last 18 months, falling as low as 79.75 percent in April 1995 and then recovering to its current 113 yen.
Helmut Schlesinger, a former Bundesbank president, agreed a new system was necessary, but expressed concern about how the target zones would be decided and ranges maintained.
"Shouldn't we keep the present system of floating exchange rates, a number of fixed systems and a number of bilateral agreements?" he said.
Schlesinger also said he was optimistic about the progress towards European Monetary Union, adding that he felt it would start as scheduled in 1999.
